codings.one_line: Grok's trending-news summary feature published unfounded claims that Trump's speech issues were due to missing dentures.
codings.rationale: Harm came from Grok's automated news-summary feature generating content from trending posts, not from a system output in an interaction with a user; fails scope conditions 1-2.

codings.one_line: Reporter's generative AI writing tool fabricated quotes from Wyoming officials; stories ran, forcing retractions and his resignation.
codings.rationale: Ordinary drafting requests to a chatbot produced fabricated quotes that were relied upon (C test: input would pass as legitimate use). Documented harm was retractions, apologies, and resignation, with no legal or regulatory action.

codings.one_line: Samsung engineers pasted confidential source code and meeting notes into ChatGPT, leaking trade secrets to OpenAI.
codings.rationale: Harm arose from confidential data being entered and retained, a data-leak/confidentiality issue; no model output in an interaction caused the harm, so it fails scope condition 2.

codings.one_line: Microsoft Copilot falsely described court reporter Martin Bernklau as a child abuser and fraudster and gave out his home address.
codings.rationale: Asking a search chatbot who a named person is would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic (C test); the system confabulated crimes he had covered. Harm was defamation and distress; criminal complaints were rejected and no suit was filed, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Copilot, asked for fictional workplace-training case studies, output the real name and case details of a sexual harassment complainant.
codings.rationale: The trainer's request for a fictional case study was ordinary, good-faith use (C test); the system regurgitated real identifying details. Documented harm was distress and privacy exposure with no legal/financial consequence attributed to the output.

codings.one_line: AI-generated fake quotes from real film critics trashing Coppola's earlier films appeared in Lionsgate's Megalopolis trailer.
codings.rationale: The input, replicated by Variety, was a plain-language request for negative critic quotes about Coppola's work, ordinary use that failed via fabrication (C test). Harm was embarrassment, a pulled trailer, and a dropped consultant; no legal or financial action documented.

codings.one_line: LAUSD's $6M 'Ed' chatbot project collapsed when vendor AllHere failed financially; the founder was later charged with fraud.
codings.rationale: The documented harm stems from vendor financial collapse and investor fraud, not from any chatbot output or action in a user interaction; fails scope condition 2.

codings.one_line: Child protection worker drafted a Children's Court report with ChatGPT; output downplayed risk to a child and leaked case data.
codings.rationale: The worker used ChatGPT for ordinary drafting assistance and the output contained inaccuracies that downplayed harm (C test: routine task input). OVIC found IPP contraventions and issued a compliance notice, a regulatory consequence, so enforceable.

codings.one_line: A Character.ai user created an unauthorized chatbot avatar of 2006 murder victim Jennifer Crecente; the platform removed it.
codings.rationale: The harm was a third party's unauthorized impersonation/creation of a synthetic persona; no harmful system output in a documented interaction caused the harm, so it fails scope condition 2.

codings.one_line: Character.ai companion bot engaged a 14-year-old in romantic chats and reinforced his suicidal intent; he died by suicide.
codings.rationale: The teen used the companion app as intended, disclosing feelings and suicidal thoughts in ordinary conversation (C test); the bot's replies reinforced his intent. A wrongful-death lawsuit was filed, so harm is enforceable.
